title: Enterprise Architecture
description: An enterprise architecture: the strategic objectives that drive it, the business value horizons that frame it, the clients and tiers that compose it, the components and contracts within each tier, and the directional flows connecting them

title.description: The name or subject of the enterprise architecture

Objectives.description: The strategic business objectives driving the architecture

Horizons.description: The business value horizons classifying the architecture's tiers

Horizon.description: One business value horizon framing an architectural tier

name.description: The display title of the horizon

tenets.description: The guiding principles, characteristics, or constraints of this horizon

HorizonId.description: The identifier of a business value horizon

Clients.description: The external and internal actors that interact with enterprise solutions

name.description: The display name of the client layer

audiences.description: The distinct groups of users or consumers

description.description: Prose explaining the client roles and access modes

Tiers.description: The architectural tiers composing the enterprise topology

id.description: The stable identifier for the tier

horizon.description: The business value horizon this tier belongs to

description.description: The purpose and scope of the tier

tenets.description: The specific tenets and operating principles of this tier

components.description: The services, tools, streams, or data stores within this tier

contracts.description: The interface contracts, protocols, or capture points exposed or consumed by this tier

Component.description: One architectural building block within a tier: a service, stream, application, COTS system, or data store

id.description: The unique identifier of the component

name.description: The display name of the component

kind.description: The functional classification of the component

description.description: The role and behavior of the component

contracts.description: Identifiers of contracts this component provides or binds to

status.description: The lifecycle state of the component

ComponentStatus.description: The lifecycle status of the component: active, planned, or decommission-asap

Contract.description: An interface boundary or contract governing interaction with components in a tier

id.description: The unique identifier of the contract

name.description: The display name of the contract

description.description: The specification or purpose of the contract

Flows.description: The directional interactions and data flows crossing tier and component boundaries

Flow.description: One directional interaction between architectural tiers or components

from.description: The identifier of the source tier or component

to.description: The identifier of the target tier or component

contract.description: The contract governing this interaction, if applicable

description.description: What is exchanged across the boundary

FlowPattern.description: The communication pattern connecting source and target

Rules.description: Architectural rules and constraints enforced across the enterprise

id.description: The name or handle of the rule

tier.description: The tier the rule applies to, or all tiers if omitted

body.description: The normative requirement of the rule

examples.title: Enterprise Architecture
objectives: Adoption of artificial intelligence done right
Reduce the cost of introducing new capabilities

horizons.name: Tactical
tenets: Isolated, one solution cannot be dependent on another solution

clients.name: Clients - Customers, Partners and Internal Users
clients.description: Clients accessing enterprise applications and orchestration tools

tiers.name: Solution Tier
tiers.description: Tactical layer delivering fast-to-market business capabilities and user experiences
tenets: Isolated, one solution cannot be dependent on another solution

components.name: Applications and Orchestration Tools
components.description: End-user applications and workflow orchestration tools

contracts.name: User Interfaces and External Rest APIs
contracts.description: Perimeter interfaces exposing web, mobile, and REST entry points to clients

tiers.name: Domain Tier
tiers.description: Strategic layer encapsulating core enterprise business logic and durable domain capabilities

components.name: Domain Services
components.description: Core reusable business services exposing domain capabilities through REST API contracts

components.name: Third Party COTS or Services
components.description: Pluggable third-party commercial off-the-shelf software or SaaS integrated behind domain boundaries

contracts.name: Rest APIs Contracts
contracts.description: Versioned REST contracts defining domain service boundaries

tiers.name: Data Mesh Tier
tiers.description: Governed data product layer publishing persistent, immutable business facts and curated streams

components.name: Curated Event and Entity Streams
components.description: Governed analytical and operational event and entity streams

components.name: Legacy Data Streams
components.description: Streams ingested from legacy datastores via data capture mechanisms

contracts.name: Event Contracts
contracts.description: Schema-governed contracts defining structure and semantics of published business events

contracts.name: Legacy Data Capture
contracts.description: Ingestion interface capturing changes and records from legacy persistence systems

tiers.name: Legacy Tier
tiers.description: Existing legacy systems carrying operational risk and targeted for prompt decommissioning

components.name: Legacy Service
components.description: Pre-existing unmaintainable service slated for decommissioning

components.name: DB2
components.description: Legacy database store accessed solely through legacy data capture

flows.description: Clients interact with applications and external REST APIs
Solutions invoke domain services via REST API contracts
Applications consume curated event and entity streams from the data mesh
Domain services publish entity state changes and consume domain events
Domain services encapsulate and integrate pluggable third-party COTS
Legacy database changes are captured into legacy data streams

rules.body: One solution cannot be dependent on another solution
Third-party COTS must be pluggable and encapsulated behind domain service contracts
Legacy data must be accessed through curated data capture rather than direct database dependencies
High-risk legacy systems must be decommissioned as soon as possible
